column3: NASB follows the critical text; “was silent” is rendered “kept silent.”
Close to the Greek; the Old Testament phrases are in capitals.
“What does it appear to you?” is rendered “how does it seem to you?”
NASB renders “cover His face” as “blindfold Him” and “strike” as “beat Him with their fists.”
NASB follows the critical text with “Jesus the Nazarene.”
NASB lacks “and a rooster crowed,” which the critical text includes in brackets.
NASB renders “those having been standing by” as “the bystanders.”
NASB follows the critical text without “and your speech shows it.”
NASB follows the critical text (“how Jesus had made the remark”); “having broken down he was weeping” is rendered “he began to weep.”
